post.title: The God Of The Old Is The Same God Of The New | Hebrews 1:1
post.description:
Contrary to what some would have us believe, the God we see in the Old is the same we see in the New Testament.

The balance in understanding the nature of God is in being acquainted with both his love and his holiness. With his goodness and his wrath.

slides.title:
The God of the Old
Is the Same God
of the *New*.
slides.sub: Some would have you believe Christ arrived to replace a harsher, older God. Hebrews 1 settles that in its opening verse.

slides.lead: Heb 1:1 summarises the connection between the Old and the New covenant.
slides.body: Contrary to what some would have us believe, the God we see in the Old is *the same* we see in the New Testament.

slides.quote: Hebrews 1:1 says it was God who"SPOKE" in times past to the fathers *THROUGH THE PROPHETS*...

slides.lead: So, before anyone will invalidate the operations of the Old Covenant as not being by God, Hebrews 1 already tells us that God is the one who spoke to the fathers in times past...
slides.body: The bible goes on to say this same God has also spoken to us *through the Son*.
It means the old testament is the revelation of God *before Christ*, while the new testament is the revelation of God *in Christ*.

slides.lead: The revelation of God in Christ would therefore not invalidate the revelation of God before Christ.
slides.body: Rather, it *sheds light on the old* so that the new will achieve the full work of salvation.

slides.lead: So, everything that the old testament scripture says God did, God really did them.
slides.body: Yes, He did them with *"His full chest."* 😁😁😁

slides.quote: Na God reason Sodom and Gomorrah matter. Na God run things inside Egypt. *Na God do all those things.*

slides.lead: The balance in understanding the nature of God is in being acquainted with both his love and his holiness.
